gen-mystery-quest-gf-cascadia-code: Nostalgic and a little bookish, Mystery Quest opens its curves wide up top, while Cascadia Code runs a thin wire-like skeleton with generous gaps. They make a loose, lively page.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads like pins standing in a wide board, its curves as heavy as its stems and its capitals blending into lowercase. And Mystery Quest above it adds bookish, open-jawed curves that keep a long page from going stiff.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa is a plain sans with wide-open curves and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height. And Oxanium brings the commanding, monoline punch up top, leaving the body to stay clear and distinct.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-julius-sans-one: That lowercase g with its open lower curve is pure Revalia, bold and expressive with round letters as heavy as its straight ones. Julius Sans One counters with a plain sans of hairline-light, widely spaced letters and almost no gap between capital and lowercase height.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-lexend-mega: Stencil-cut and loud, Snowburst One has wide bridges between letters and tall lowercase. And Lexend Mega answers in a plain sans drawn with one unvarying nib, steady where the heading is showy.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga spreads flat, single-weight linework across generous tracking, with ascenders that barely clear the x-height. And Tektur, with its pipe-cleaner strokes and outsized lowercase, gives that quiet sans-serif body a distinctive, expressive edge.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-lexend-peta: A splayed c terminal and tube-like, constant-width strokes make Tilt Neon unmistakable, with a big x-height under short ascenders. Lexend Peta takes the quieter job, a sans-serif body whose curves never thin out.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws a single-weight line like a plotter pen, with letters spaced as far apart as stepping stones. And Unica One tops it with a very large lowercase eye and commanding, daylight-filled curves.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta reads in tall-bodied small letters, widely tracked, with strokes like cut ribbon of constant width. Wallpoet sits on top as the bold heading, a wire-bent sign look with lowercase that rises high.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-montserrat-alternates: Expressive from the first line, Warnes tapers its ink strokes out before they touch and stretches its tracking wide. And Montserrat Alternates holds a plain sans body whose round letters match their stems, with a c as open as a bent paperclip.
